name: Triangles
intro: **Draw it, then label every known length and angle on the figure.** Most geometry errors are bookkeeping errors, not reasoning errors (§1).
Learn the Pythagorean triples cold — 3-4-5, 5-12-13, 7-24-25, 8-15-17, 9-40-41 — and that 13-14-15 has area 84. CAT picks its numbers from that list (§3).

qs.q: The sides of a triangle are 13, 14 and 15. Find its area.
qs.h: §3 — Heron's formula with s = 21. This particular triangle appears constantly in CAT; memorise that its area is 84.

qs.q: In a right triangle the legs are 9 and 12. The altitude to the hypotenuse is
qs.h: §7 — the area computed two ways: ½(9)(12) = ½(hypotenuse)(altitude).

qs.q: An equilateral triangle has area 36√3. Find its side.
qs.h: §3 — area = (√3/4)a². The √3 cancels, which is why the numbers look ugly but aren't.

qs.q: In triangle ABC, D is the midpoint of BC and the area of ABC is 48. The area of ABD is
qs.h: §4 — a median splits a triangle into two of equal area, regardless of shape.

qs.q: Two similar triangles have areas in the ratio 9 : 16. If the smaller has perimeter 45, find the perimeter of the larger.
qs.h: §4 — areas scale as the square of the linear ratio, so take square roots before scaling a length.
qs.s: Linear ratio = 3 : 4 ⟹ perimeter = 45 × 4/3 = 60. (Scaling by 16/9 gives 80 — the planted error.)

qs.q: The sides of a triangle are 7, 24 and 25. Its inradius is
qs.h: §5 — this is a right triangle, and for a right triangle r = (a + b − c)/2.
qs.s: 7² + 24² = 25² ⟹ right angled ⟹ r = (7 + 24 − 25)/2 = 3. (Check with r = Area/s = 84/18 … careful: s = 28, Area = 84 ⟹ r = 3 ✓)

qs.q: Find the area of a triangle with sides 9, 12 and 15.
qs.h: Check for a Pythagorean triple before reaching for Heron.

qs.q: In a right triangle, the hypotenuse is 26 and one leg is 10. Find the area.
qs.s: The other leg is 24 ⟹ area = ½(10)(24) = 120.

qs.q: In triangle ABC, DE is parallel to BC with AD : DB = 2 : 3. The ratio of the area of ADE to that of ABC is
qs.h: AD : AB is the linear ratio, and areas go as its square.
qs.s: AD : AB = 2 : 5 ⟹ area ratio = 4 : 25. (4 : 9 uses AD : DB — the planted error.)

audit: grinding through Heron or algebra where a Pythagorean triple was staring at you (§3)
scaling a length by the area ratio instead of by its square root — areas go as k², so take the root first (§4)
computing heights instead of using the same-height rule: a median always halves the area (§4)
